correctness.rationale: A direct inequality proof shows that any harmful homogeneous winner-raising change requires at least 17 voters. At equality it forces first-choice totals 6,5,6 and group size 2; transfer inequalities then yield exactly the two stated normal-form families. The embedded verifier exhausts every anonymous profile and every homogeneous change through 17 voters and reproduces exactly 252 profiles, 42 candidate-relabeling classes, and the symbolic family.

evidence: Ornstein and Norman give necessary and sufficient conditions for existence of an upward monotonicity failure in a three-candidate IRV profile and study frequency under a spatial model.
Miller gives a transparent general characterization in terms of competitiveness and majority comparisons.
Brandt, Matthäus, and Saile give a tie-independent minimal Additional Support witness with three candidates and 17 voters.
broader_coverage.reasoning: These broader results establish susceptibility and the sharp boundary size, but they do not imply the exact number of minimal homogeneous profiles or the two normal-form families without an additional equality-case analysis and count.

value.rationale: The theorem completely resolves the first tie-independent homogeneous-support boundary of a canonical voting pathology. The two-family normal form explains the minimal number 17 structurally and turns an isolated witness into an exact finite classification with natural incidence and symmetry data.
